subject: Clarify HIPAA deployment modes, BAA availability, SOC 2 & next steps
messages:
From: Arun Patel <arun@healthlynx.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: HIPAA scope & deployment questions from today

Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciated the walkthrough. A few things the legal and infra teams asked me to confirm after the call so we can decide whether to move forward with a pilot: 

- SOC 2: Are you SOC 2 Type II audited today? If so, can you share the report or a redacted summary?
- BAA availability: Is a BAA offered? Does it cover Hosted API, Dedicated, Private (VPC/on-prem)? Any limitations we should know about?
- PHI boundaries: What exactly would be considered PHI that you need to see/process/storage? For example: free-text clinical notes vs images vs file attachments.
- Deployment modes: Which modes are eligible for full-PHI workloads? We need an explicit statement we can give to our security/legal folks.
- KV cache / prompt history: How long is conversation history retained? Is it stored encrypted? Is there an option to disable KV caching for PHI-bearing requests?
- Vendor questionnaire: I can send a short vendor security questionnaire (PDF) — will someone on your security team pick this up?

If you can send the SOC2/BAA and a quick note on PHI handling and deployment eligibility, I can share with our CISO and Legal today. Happy to schedule a 30m security deep-dive next week if needed.

Best,
Arun
Director of Product, HealthLynx
arun@healthlynx.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: HIPAA scope & deployment questions from today

Arun — thanks for the clear list. Quick post-call recap and concrete next steps below.

Summary (short answers):
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II in April 2025. I am attaching the redacted report (redwood-soc2-report-2025.pdf) and will share a restricted Drive link for your security reviewers.
- BAA: We offer a BAA. For full PHI workloads we support BAA-backed deployments on Dedicated and Private (VPC / on-prem) only. Hosted API can be covered by BAA for scoped, tokenized/PII-lite use cases (we can discuss specifics), but we do not recommend Hosted for high-volume full-PHI storage/processing.
- PHI boundaries: PHI we consider in-scope: any free-text clinical notes, patient identifiers (MRN, DOB, SSN), structured PHI in prompts, and file attachments containing patient data. Image-processing/medical imaging is considered high-risk and should go to Private/on-prem unless you want to evaluate a controlled pilot.
- KV cache & history: By default we cache KV entries to speed generation; retention is configurable. For Dedicated and Private you can disable caching and set retention to 0. All persisted data is encrypted at rest; Private supports customer-managed KMS.
- Eligible modes for full-PHI: Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC / on-prem) — both support BAAs and tighter network controls. Hosted is viable only for non-identifiable or tokenized PHI and with explicit contract language.

Next steps (recommended):
1) I will send: SOC2 redacted PDF + our BAA template (attached).
2) Mina (cc'd) will pick up the vendor questionnaire and can coordinate a technical deep-dive.
3) If HealthLynx wants to proceed, we can provision a short Dedicated trial with retention and caching config locked down for PHI testing.

Proposed meeting times: Tue 11/10 10am PT or Wed 11/11 1pm PT — please choose what works for your team.

Attaching: redwood-soc2-report-2025.pdf; redwood-baa-template.docx

Thanks,
Karthik

karthik@redwood.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: HIPAA scope & deployment questions from today

Arun / team — quick technical notes from security so your infra/legal folks have actionable answers. Happy to go deeper on the call.

PHI handling boundaries (detailed):
- In-scope PHI: any unredacted patient identifiers or clinical free text you send to the API or store in our retention layers (prompts, completions, system messages, attachments).
- Attachments: We treat file attachments that contain PHI (PDFs, images with burned-in PHI) as in-scope and recommend Private or on-prem for those workloads. Attachments are not sent to model-hosting partners unless explicitly configured.
- KV cache: KV entries are used to speed next-token generation; by default they are encrypted with our platform key. For Dedicated you can disable KV caching globally or per-route. On Private you can choose customer KMS and full cache isolation.
- Encryption & keys: Transit TLS 1.3; at rest AES-256. Customer-managed KMS (CMK) available for Private. Dedicated supports CMK in most cloud regions — we will confirm for your preferred region.
- Data retention: Configurable per-deployment. For PHI pilots we recommend retention=0 (no persistent storage of prompts/completions) and request-level logging only for error trace with PII redaction.
- Model variants & inference routing: We can route PHI-bearing requests to quantized/evaluated model variants that run only on Dedicated/Private pools. Fallback to Hosted is blocked for routes tagged PHI.

Vendor questionnaire: Please send the PDF. I will triage and return answers within 3 business days. If there are cryptographic or network diagrams needed, I will attach them.

Deliverables I will share after this thread:
- Restricted SOC 2 summary link (redacted)
- BAA template (Word) with our security annex
- Short architecture diagram showing PHI dataflow for Dedicated & Private

If you want us to pre-populate your questionnaire, attach it in reply and mark any high-priority questions.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com
